newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Merrill sees buoyant HK residential property mart.
newsitem.headline: Merrill sees buoyant HK residential property mart.

text.p: Hong Kong's residential property market should remain buoyant in the next two years in line with the territory's positive economic outlook, Merrill Lynch said in a report on Tuesday.

"We feel that the negative influence exerted by a possible U.S. credit tightening on the local bourse should be diluted by a promising economic outlook for both Hong Kong and China," Merrill Lynch said.
"In addition, we think that the improved fundamentals of the residential sector should remain intact."

A recovery in transaction volumes, a growing population, improved affordability, abundant liquidity, tight supply, expansion of urban renewal and an optimistic outlook for the luxury sector supported the conclusion that selected property development stocks would continue to show good value for money, Merrill Lynch said in its report.

Three of the companies that stood to benefit most from this trend were Henderson Land Development Co, SHK Properties and New World Development Co, given their significant exposure to this sector and their attractive discounts to net asset value, the report said.
Merrill Lynch noted that residential prices had risen about 16 percent in the year to date and were about 20 percent higher than the trough in third-quarter 1995.
The rise in the primary market was even stronger at about 30 percent to 40 percent higher than prices in the trough, it said.
"Nevertheless, we believe the mass sector may see another 8-12 percent gain in capital values per annum in the coming two years," Merrill Lynch said.
